name: U.S. Outpatient Influenza-like Illness Surveillance Network
reports: The weekly percentage of outpatient visits meeting the influenza-like illness definition, reported by age group.
interpretation: A timely syndromic signal of respiratory illness. It is not laboratory-confirmed influenza and can include other pathogens.

name: National Syndromic Surveillance Program
reports: The percentage of emergency-department visits with an influenza discharge diagnosis, overall and by age group.
interpretation: A near-real-time signal from most U.S. emergency departments; it reflects care-seeking, testing, and diagnostic coding.

name: Influenza Hospitalization Surveillance Network
reports: Population-based weekly rates and detailed characteristics of laboratory-confirmed influenza hospitalizations in selected catchment areas.
interpretation: Rich clinical detail and a defined population denominator, but the network covers about 10% of the U.S. population and recent weeks are revised.

name: National Healthcare Safety Network Hospital Respiratory Data Module
reports: Weekly facility-level counts of new laboratory-confirmed influenza admissions, current hospitalizations, ICU occupancy, and bed capacity.
interpretation: Broad national hospital coverage and operational situational awareness, using aggregated facility reports.

name: U.S. Influenza Collaborating Laboratories System
reports: Influenza-positive specimens by virus type, subtype or lineage, and age; selected viruses undergo genetic, antigenic, and antiviral-susceptibility characterization.
interpretation: Best for identifying which viruses are circulating and how they are changing, not for estimating community positivity.

name: National Respiratory and Enteric Virus Surveillance System
reports: The weekly number of respiratory specimens tested, number positive, and percent positive for influenza by virus type.
interpretation: Clinical laboratory testing helps show the timing and intensity of influenza circulation.

name: National Center for Health Statistics Mortality Surveillance
reports: Weekly death-certificate measures for deaths coded with influenza, pneumonia, and/or COVID-19.
interpretation: A national mortality signal that is delayed and repeatedly revised; influenza-only coding underestimates influenza's full mortality burden.

name: Influenza-Associated Pediatric Mortality Surveillance System
reports: Individual laboratory-confirmed influenza-associated deaths among people younger than 18 years, with demographic and clinical details.
interpretation: A nationally notifiable severe outcome. Counts are small, case-based, and can arrive after investigation and confirmation.
